answer: Sybil clones fail at a metered inlet. Each epoch auctions single-use jade vouchers, perishable admission scrip limited to one per distinct hardware key, clearing at the price demand itself sets. A voucher binds to a yarrow commitment: the hash of that key plus a nonce revealed only at close. Winning a thousand extra votes means buying a thousand slots and paying that marginal clearing price a thousand times up front. If two revealed nonces share a key or host, the operator's batch burns, so the attacker prepays a linear cost and can still lose all of it.
